sections.label: Background
sections.text: Prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography (PSMA-PET) improves lesion detection, leading to treatment intensification via PSMA-guided radiotherapy (PSMAgRT), but its impact on patient outcomes remains undefined.

sections.label: Objective
sections.text: We evaluated whether PSMAgRT improves failure-free survival (FFS).

sections.label: Design, setting, and participants
sections.text: This phase 2, two-center, open-label randomized trial enrolled patients planned for standard-of-care (SOC) radiotherapy (RT).

sections.label: Intervention
sections.text: Patients were randomized 1:1 to SOC or PSMAgRT to all detected sites across four strata: salvage post-radical prostatectomy (RP), high-risk, oligometastatic, and salvage post-RT. Between 2018 and 2021, 262 patients were randomized (253 treated/analyzed).

sections.label: Outcome measurements and statistical analysis
sections.text: The primary FFS end point (measured from RT completion) comprised prostate-specific antigen (PSA)/radiological progression, next-line therapy, or death. Secondary end points included freedom from biochemical progression (FFBP; PSA rise ≥0.2 ng/ml post-RP or ≥2 ng/ml above nadir in other strata). Prespecified analyses used a one-sided threshold of p1 < 0.10, whereas post hoc analyses used two-sided p < 0.05 thresholds and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

sections.label: Results and limitations
sections.text: Among 253 patients, median follow-up was 66 mo (range 9-91). The 5-yr primary FFS was 66% with PSMAgRT versus 62% in controls (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.80; one-sided 90% CI, upper bound 1.04; p1 = 0.14). FFBP favored PSMAgRT: 72% versus 65% overall (subdistribution HR [sHR] 0.70, one-sided 90% CI upper bound 0.92; p1 = 0.048), 81% versus 66% in patients with high-risk disease (sHR 0.54; p1 = 0.07), and 80% versus 68% in patients in post-RP stratum (sHR 0.54; p1 = 0.037). In an exploratory, post hoc analysis combining patients with high-risk disease and those in the post-RP stratum, FFBP favored PSMAgRT (sHR 0.54, 95% CI = 0.32-0.91; two-sided p = 0.02). Only one grade ≥3 event was possibly related to dose escalation. Limitations include a phase 2 design with a heterogeneous population.

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: Although the primary FFS end point was not met in the overall population, treatment-effect estimates favored PSMAgRT in the high-risk and post-RP strata. These findings provide a meaningful rationale for the target populations currently being evaluated in the definitive phase 3 PATRON trial.

43020696.title: Diagnostic Performance of Nectin-4-targeted [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT versus [18F]-FDG PET/CT for Staging of Locally Advanced and Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma: A Prospective, Single-center, Phase 2 Feasibility Trial.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT is feasible for whole-body nectin-4 assessment in la/mUC and supports a distinct biodistribution from FDG, suggesting complementary rather than interchangeable roles. Further prospective evaluation with treatment-outcome correlation is warranted before its use as a biomarker to guide EV-based therapy selection.

sections.text: Enfortumab vedotin (EV), an anti-nectin-4 antibody-drug conjugate, alone and with pembrolizumab (EV plus pembrolizumab [EV/P]), has transformed the treatment of locally advanced/metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC), yet remains biomarker agnostic. We prospectively evaluated [68Ga]Ga-DOTA-N188 PET/CT ([68Ga]-N188 PET/CT) as a whole-body alternative for nectin-4 imaging, with [18F]-FDG PET/CT as an active comparator and conventional computed tomography as the reference standard for staging la/mUC in 25 patients planned for EV/P. [18F]-FDG PET/CT showed a higher maximum standardized uptake value and tumor-to-background ratio than [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT across most lesion types (primary tumor, visceral, and osseous), except for lymph nodes. The overall tracer correlation was weak (Spearman r = 0.196), strongest in lymph nodes (r = 0.657), and absent in primary tumors and bone lesions. For primary tumor detection, [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT had higher specificity (86% vs 57%) and positive predictive value (92% vs 83%) than FDG, which had higher sensitivity (88% vs 67%). Nodal staging performance was similar in the tracers. For distant metastases, both achieved 100% sensitivity and negative predictive value, with [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT showing marginally higher specificity. [68Ga]-N188 PET/CT is feasible for whole-body nectin-4 assessment in la/mUC and supports a distinct biodistribution from FDG, suggesting complementary rather than interchangeable roles. Further prospective evaluation with treatment-outcome correlation is warranted before its use as a biomarker to guide EV-based therapy selection.

42384203.title: Redefining robotic image-guidance - tomographic visualization of lesions during prostate cancer surgery via gantry-free robotic SPECT.
42384203.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
42384203.journal_full: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
42384203.authors: Berrens AC, Pirkovets K, Azargoshasb S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: RoboSPECT provides 3D context that extends the utility of drop-in gamma tracing and assists the alignment between pre- and intra-operative target perception. Here SN-RoboSPECT clearly outperformed fluorescence SN imaging and PSMA-RoboSPECT outperformed preoperative PSMA-SPECT/CT imaging.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: The introduction of the drop-in gamma probe has advanced intraoperative molecular imaging during prostate cancer surgery. We have been able to convert the sensor's numeric readout to tomographic images, so-called robotic-SPECT (RoboSPECT) and investigate how this is impacted by radiopharmaceutical avidities and drop-in scan metrics.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: The gamma sensor readout was registered with its 3D position and orientation, allowing a custom reconstruction algorithm to generate RoboSPECT images. Evaluations occurred in 21 patients; 10 sentinel node procedures (SN; primary prostate cancer) and 11 PSMA-radioguided surgery (recurrent prostate cancer). RoboSPECT findings were related to respective pre- and intra-operative controls, including preoperative PSMA-PET/CT and/or SPECT/CT images and fluorescence detection (SN only).

sections.label: Results
sections.text: RoboSPECT proved to be safe and applicable in a range of conditions. In the SN-group, 26 SN-SPECT/CT lesions were successfully identified with SN-RoboSPECT (100%); 3 were tumor positive (sensitivity 100%). Only 73% of SNs were surgically visible with fluorescence imaging. For the PSMA guided group, the 14 lesions identified on PSMA-PET/CT were all visualized with PSMA-RoboSPECT (100%); 18 specimens were tumor positive (sensitivity 78% for both PSMA-PET/CT and PSMA-RoboSPECT). Preoperative PSMA-SPECT/CT only identified 4 PSMA-lesions (29%). No false positives were seen for roboSPECT and all final resection margins were clean. At 6-months 0% of the SN-patients and 20% of PSMA-patients showed biochemical recurrence.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: RoboSPECT provides 3D context that extends the utility of drop-in gamma tracing and assists the alignment between pre- and intra-operative target perception. Here SN-RoboSPECT clearly outperformed fluorescence SN imaging and PSMA-RoboSPECT outperformed preoperative PSMA-SPECT/CT imaging.

42599911.title: Shear wave elastography demonstrates similar risk stratification performance to vibration-controlled transient elastography in FIB-4-based two-step algorithms for MASLD.
42599911.authors: Lee J, Yang H, Bae SH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: SWE-based two-step risk stratification showed similar predictive performance to VCTE-based models for predicting LREs in MASLD, although these findings do not establish formal equivalence.

sections.label: Background and aims
sections.text: The role of shear wave elastography (SWE) in two-step MASLD risk stratification remains unclear. We compared SWE with vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) using American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) algorithms.

sections.label: Approach and results
sections.text: Patients with MASLD who underwent both VCTE and SWE during the same session between 2019 and 2025 were included. Risk stratification was performed using AGA-based and EASL-based two-step approaches. The primary endpoint was liver-related events (LREs). Among 2817 patients, the AGA-SWE algorithm classified 2196, 140, and 481 patients as low-risk, intermediate-risk, and high-risk, respectively. Using the AGA-SWE algorithm, both intermediate-risk and high-risk groups showed increased risks of LREs compared with the low-risk group [subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 7.60 and 9.86, respectively]. The EASL-SWE algorithm also stratified LRE risk relative to the low-risk group, with higher sHRs observed for the intermediate-low, intermediate-high, and high-risk groups (sHR 2.99, 10.83, and 18.87, respectively). The integrated time-dependent area under the curve through 60 months was 0.770 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.709, 0.827] and 0.775 (95% CI: 0.712, 0.835) for AGA-SWE and AGA-VCTE, respectively, and 0.804 (95% CI: 0.753, 0.849) and 0.805 (95% CI: 0.750, 0.852) for EASL-SWE and EASL-VCTE, respectively, with no significant differences between SWE and VCTE in either algorithm. No significant net reclassification improvement was observed between SWE-based and VCTE-based AGA algorithms. SWE and VCTE demonstrated a strong correlation (Spearman ρ = 0.713, 95% CI: 0.691-0.735, p <0.001).

sections.label: Conclusions
sections.text: SWE-based two-step risk stratification showed similar predictive performance to VCTE-based models for predicting LREs in MASLD, although these findings do not establish formal equivalence.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To determine the degree of tumor necrosis on pathology and clinical outcomes among intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) patients who were treated with transarterial radioembolization (TARE) and the bridge or downstaged to surgery.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: A single center retrospective review was performed to include consecutive patients who underwent TARE using glass microspheres and then subsequently underwent surgical resection or transplant. Baseline characteristics, dosimetry, radiologic response, histological tumor necrosis, and overall survival were evaluated. A total of 20 patients (F: M = 14:6; age: 57.3 ± 10.8 years) underwent TARE and then received resection (n = 15) or living-donor liver transplant (n = 5). A total of 23 selective TARE (two segments or less) were delivered, with a mean dose 301.7 ± 177.5, whereas 18 lobar (left or right hepatic artery) doses were delivered, with a mean dose of 150.3 ± 44.1 Gy. Concurrent systemic therapy was administered in 15 patients.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: The mean time from the initial TARE to surgery was 7.1 ± 9.2 months. On pathology, complete tumor necrosis, > 90% necrosis, and extensive tumor necrosis (> 50%) were achieved in 1 (5.0%), 13 (65.0%), and 18 (90.0%) patients, respectively. The median survival time (MST) calculated from the time of surgery was 40.2 (95%CI: 15.3-not reached) months, with a 1-yr, 3-yr, and 5-yr OS of 88.2% (95CI: 60.6-96.9%), 57.8% (95%CI: 31.1-77.3%), and 19.8% (95%CI: 1.5-53.5%). From the time of initial TARE, the MST was 41.4 (95%CI:22.9-not reached) month, with a 1-yr, 3-yr, and 5-yr OS of 100%, 69.9% (95%CI: 42.0-86.3%), and 30.9% (95%CI: 9.1-56.3%). Whether the patient received concomitant systemic treatment was associated with extensive tumor necrosis on pathology (Odds Ratio: 16.0, 95%CI: 1.27-200.92, p = 0.032).

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Based on tumor explant data, TARE can result in substantial tumor necrosis in the treatment of iCCA, although complete necrosis is uncommon. The addition of systemic therapy appears to be associated with a higher likelihood of achieving extensive tumor necrosis.

42836755.title: Perfusion beyond Margin in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Contrast-enhanced US Feature Related to Tumor Invasiveness and Prognosis.
42836755.authors: Ding W, Ji R, Pang C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Perfusion beyond margin, a new imaging feature, was identified through contrast-enhanced US in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma; it was associated with greater invasive potential and poorer prognosis.

sections.text: Background Previous studies on imaging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have shown inconsistency in the growth of tumor vascularity and gross morphologic features. Contrast-enhanced US (CEUS) is one of the few methods that can depict both features simultaneously, making it valuable for assessing this inconsistency and its potential clinical influence. Purpose To evaluate and establish a new CEUS feature representing inconsistency between vascularity and gross morphologic features (perfusion beyond margin [PBM]) and analyze its underlying biologic mechanisms and prognostic influence. Materials and Methods This multicenter retrospective study included patients with HCC from January 2015 to August 2023. Three radiologists (5-8 years of experience) measured tumor diameter using gray-scale US and CEUS. Mathematic, prognostic, and bioinformatics analyses were used to quantify the PBM diagnostic standard. Prognostic analysis included recurrence-free survival after laparoscopic hepatectomy and local tumor progression-free survival after thermal ablation. Bioinformatics analysis included pathologic and immunohistochemical evaluation and RNA sequencing. Results This study included 1076 patients (mean age ± SD, 60 years ± 10.5; 854 men, 1166 HCCs). PBM was defined as the tumor diameter on arterial phase exceeding that at gray-scale US by 5 mm. PBM was associated with worse recurrence-free survival (hazard ratio [HR], 1.76 [95% CI: 1.05, 2.94]; P = .03); worse local tumor progression-free survival (HR, 2.40 [95% CI: 1.84, 3.13]; P < .001); and higher rates of microvascular invasion (52.2% [12 of 23] vs 25.0% [29 of 116]; P = .02), cytokeratin-7 positivity (26.2% [11 of 42] vs 11.3% [14 of 124]; P = .04), and cytokeratin-19 positivity (26.9% [seven of 26] vs 8.8% [13 of 148]; P = .02) compared with the non-PBM group. PBM occurrence was related to upregulation of genes for angiogenesis (VEGA, PIGF), epithelial-mesenchymal transition (TGFB1, MMP2), and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (CD163). PBM was more common in patients with cirrhosis (26.8% [236 of 880]; P = .04; odds ratio, 1.41), recurrent tumors (28.4% [161 of 567]; P = .02; odds ratio, 1.38), and tumors greater than 3 cm (30.8% [92 of 298]; P = .01; odds ratio, 1.46). Conclusion Perfusion beyond margin, a new imaging feature, was identified through contrast-enhanced US in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma; it was associated with greater invasive potential and poorer prognosis.

42867371.title: Artificial Intelligence for Prostate Cancer Detection and Screening on MRI in Global Populations: The SCARLET-1 Study.
42867371.authors: Saha A, Bosma JS, Twilt JJ, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: AI demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of radiology readings across external diagnostic and screening datasets.

sections.text: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have demonstrated non-inferiority to radiologists for prostate cancer detection on MRI, but evidence in global diagnostic and population-based screening settings remains limited. Purpose To determine whether an AI system can achieve diagnostic performance comparable to radiology readings for detecting Gleason grade group ≥2 prostate cancer on MRI in external diagnostic and screening datasets. Materials and Methods In the SCARLET-1 retrospective validation study, prostate MRIs from adults with suspected prostate cancer (January 2012-October 2024) were used to evaluate an AI system, with external testing in diagnostic (PRIME) and organized screening settings (STHLM3-MRI and IP1-PROSTAGRAM). The primary outcome was agreement between AI assessments and standard-of-care diagnoses of Gleason grade group ≥2 cancer, with diagnostic interchangeability defined relative to the estimated agreement of an average radiologist. Secondary outcomes included area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) across datasets and subgroups. Results 22,445 examinations (21,252 male patients; median age, 66 years [IQR 60-71]) were included: 20,471 prostate MRI examinations (19,278 patients; 26 cities, 14 countries) for AI training and internal testing, and 1974 patients (20 external cities, 12 countries) for external testing. External AUCs were 0.86 (95% CI: 0.83, 0.90) in PRIME, 0.89 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.92) in STHLM3-MRI, and 0.84 (95% CI: 0.70, 0.95) in IP1-PROSTAGRAM. The primary outcome was 83.0% (395 of 476; adjusted 95% CI: 78.8%, 87.0%), 87.9% (974 of 1108; adjusted 95% CI: 85.6%, 90.3%), and 87.7% (342 of 390; adjusted 95% CI: 83.6%, 91.5%), respectively, meeting prespecified interchangeability criteria in all datasets. Subgroup performance was consistent across age, risk, cancer location and ethnicity (mean ΔAUC, 0.02), but varied substantially across 25 sites (28% with AUC<0.80; 32% with AUC ≥0.90) and by image quality (AUC, 0.78-0.88). Conclusion AI demonstrated diagnostic performance comparable to that of radiology readings across external diagnostic and screening datasets.

42899938.title: Intraindividual Comparison of Radiation Dose and Image Quality: Photon-counting versus Energy-integrating Detector CT in Obesity.
42899938.authors: Hegmanns J, Zensen S, Rosok D, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In patients with obesity, intraindividual comparisons demonstrated that PCCT had superior quantitative and subjective image quality at a lower radiation dose than EID CT.

sections.text: Background Maintaining diagnostic CT image quality in patients with obesity remains challenging because increased x-ray attenuation is often offset by higher radiation exposure. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) has demonstrated improved dose efficiency and image quality, but intraindividual data in this population are limited. Purpose To compare radiation dose, quantitative image quality, and subjective image quality between PCCT and energy-integrating detector (EID) CT intraindividually in patients with obesity. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included patients with obesity undergoing thoracic and/or abdominal CT at both PCCT and EID CT between December 1, 2022, and January 31, 2025. Signal, image noise, and signal to noise ratio (SNR) were measured in vascular, parenchymal, muscular, and adipose tissue. Two radiologists independently rated image quality on a six-point Likert scale. Radiation dose parameters were volume CT dose index (CTDIvol), dose-length product (DLP), and effective dose. The paired two-sided t test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used for group comparisons. Results This study included 51 patients with obesity (median age, 56 years [IQR, 51-66.5 years]; 33 male). Signal was higher with PCCT than EID CT in vascular structures, parenchymal organs, and muscle and more negative in subcutaneous fat (all P < .001), with similar image noise (P = .09-.84). SNR was higher with PCCT in vascular structures (ascending aorta: mean, 19.65 ± 6.47 [SD] vs 13.22 ± 4.83; P < .001) and most parenchymal organs (liver: 5.53 ± 1.69 vs 4.71 ± 1.89; P = .02). The difference in SNR increased with body mass index for vessels (r = 0.36) and parenchymal organs (r = 0.51) (both P < .001). Both readers rated overall image quality, contrast, and sharpness higher and artifact-related impairment lower for PCCT (all P < .001), whereas subjective image noise was similar (P = .16 and .14). CTDIvol (median, 11.99 vs 17.05 mGy) and DLP (median, 526.25 vs 709.32 mGy · cm) were lower with PCCT (both P < .001). Conclusion In patients with obesity, intraindividual comparisons demonstrated that PCCT had superior quantitative and subjective image quality at a lower radiation dose than EID CT.

42937537.title: US Markers in the Noninvasive Assessment of Hepatic Steatosis in Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
42937537.authors: Sugimoto K, Moriyasu F, Dioguardi Burgio M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Liver US-derived AC performed better than NLV and hepatorenal ratio in determining steatosis grade in participants with MASLD; when these markers were combined, reclassification of steatosis grade improved.

sections.text: Background Attenuation coefficient (AC) is an established US marker for assessing patients with liver steatosis. However, improvements in diagnostic performance are warranted. Purpose To evaluate the diagnostic performance of AC, normalized local variance (NLV), hepatorenal ratio, and their combinations for liver histopathologic steatosis in participants with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Materials and Methods This secondary analysis of the prospective Innovative Liver Elasticity, Attenuation, and Dispersion Ultrasound Study (iLEAD) (June 2019 to March 2023) included participants with biopsy-proven MASLD who underwent multiparametric liver US; AC, NLV, and hepatorenal ratio were measured. The diagnostic performance of each imaging marker and their combinations for determining steatosis grade were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with the DeLong test, and reclassification improvement was also assessed using the category-free net reclassification improvement (NRI). Results A total of 102 participants (mean age, 52 years ± 16.1 [SD]; 51 male) were evaluated. AC showed the highest diagnostic performance for determining steatosis grade across all grades (AUC for grade ≥S1, 0.93 [95% CI: 0.87, 0.99]), compared with NLV (0.88 [95% CI: 0.77, 0.99]; P = .47) and hepatorenal ratio (0.85 [95% CI: 0.71, 0.98]; P = .30). Four models were constructed for identifying steatosis grades: model 1, AC only; model 2, AC plus NLV; model 3, AC plus hepatorenal ratio; model 4, AC plus NLV plus hepatorenal ratio. Models 2-4 showed no evidence of a difference in performance from model 1 for identifying grade S1 or higher (AUC, 0.93-0.98; P = .16, .15, and .07, respectively), but an improvement in risk reclassification was observed for model 4 (NRI, 1.18 [95% CI: 0.54, 1.77]; P < .001) compared with model 1 (reference). Performance was similar across models in identifying steatosis grade S2 or greater (AUC, 0.89-0.90; all P ≥ .47) and for grade S3 (AUC, 0.89-0.90; all P ≥ .72), but an improvement in risk reclassification was observed for model 3 compared with model 1 (≥S2 steatosis: NRI, 0.58 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.94] [P = .002]; S3 steatosis: NRI, 0.71 [95% CI: 0.26, 1.14] [P = .002]). Conclusion Liver US-derived AC performed better than NLV and hepatorenal ratio in determining steatosis grade in participants with MASLD; when these markers were combined, reclassification of steatosis grade improved.

43043182.title: Histotripsy versus Established Thermal Ablation Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of FDA MAUDE Adverse Event Reporting Patterns.
43043182.authors: Kundu A, Tam A, Zhao L, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation.

sections.text: Background Histotripsy recently received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance for liver tumors, but long-term safety data remain limited. Purpose To characterize histotripsy-related adverse events (AEs) reported to the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database during the early postmarket period and contextualize findings in comparison to microwave ablation (MWA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) during comparable observation windows. Materials and Methods A retrospective analysis of the FDA MAUDE database was conducted. AE reports were analyzed over comparable 24-month postmarket periods: July 2024 to July 2026 for histotripsy, January 2017 to January 2019 for MWA, and January 2016 to January 2018 for RFA. Reports were classified by severity (malfunction, serious injury, and death) and medical problem category. Firth-penalized reporting odds ratios (RORs), relative risks (RRs), and Bayesian modeling using Bass model-derived procedure volumes enabled exploratory denominator-adjusted comparisons. Results Of 570 AE reports initially identified, 506 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis (71 histotripsy [median patient age, 68 years; IQR, 56-76 years] and 435 MWA/RFA [median patient age, 58 years; IQR, 50-67 years]). Serious injury and death occurred in 86% (61 of 71) and 14% (10 of 71) of histotripsy reports versus 20% (89 of 435) and 2% (eight of 435) of MWA/RFA reports. Histotripsy had higher reported odds of serious injury (ROR, 14.24 [95% CI: 6.29, 35.56]; P < .001) and death (ROR, 4.35 [95% CI: 1.08, 24.35]; P = .04). In exploratory analyses using modeled procedure volumes, estimated RRs based on reported events were 6.11 (95% CI: 2.64, 14.11; P < .001) for serious injury and 10.94 (95% CI: 4.73, 25.33; P < .001) for death. Although sparse event counts produced imprecise estimates for some complication categories, histotripsy showed higher reporting odds of renal and urinary complications (P < .001), hemorrhage and vascular injury (P < .001), and gastrointestinal and/or abdominal complications (P < .001) in the full cohort. A sensitivity analysis excluding malfunction-only reports showed similar organ system reporting patterns. Conclusion Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation.

42813999.title: Deep Learning Analysis of Dual-Modality US Videos for the Characterization of Superficial Lymphadenopathy.
42813999.authors: Zhu Y, Cao R, Zhu Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: DMUVL-DiagNet enabled accurate characterization of superficial LA and improved junior radiologist diagnostic performance. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry no. ChiCTR2400090592

sections.text: Purpose To develop and validate a deep learning (DL) model based on dual-modality US videos to differentiate benign from malignant superficial lymphadenopathy (LA) and stratify malignant subtypes. Materials and Methods This multicenter study included patients with pathologically confirmed LA from five centers (June 2019-December 2025). The Dual-Modality US Video Lymphadenopathy Diagnostic Network (DMUVL-DiagNet) model integrated B-mode and color Doppler flow imaging videos with basic clinical information. A retrospective video dataset (n = 1616) was used for training and internal testing, and external testing used a prospective dual-modality US video set (n = 454) and a static US image set (n = 1956). Model performance was compared against clinical baseline and US-based DL models, and an artificial intelligence-assisted reader study was conducted. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) were calculated to evaluate diagnostic performance. Results Overall, 4026 patients (median age, 52.6 years [IQR, 41-62]; 2175 male, 1851 female) were included. DMUVL-DiagNet consistently outperformed clinical and US-based models across all test sets, achieving AUCs of 0.91-0.95 for benign versus malignant classification and 0.87-0.91 for lymphoma versus metastasis classification. The model showed good generalizability (subgroup AUCs, 0.85-0.93) and surpassed the average performance of all radiologist experience groups in both tasks. Additionally, DMUVL-DiagNet assistance improved junior radiologist AUCs from 0.72 to 0.88 and from 0.58 to 0.77 for the two tasks, respectively (all P < .001). Conclusion DMUVL-DiagNet enabled accurate characterization of superficial LA and improved junior radiologist diagnostic performance. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry no. ChiCTR2400090592

42949521.title: Anatomy-informed CT Spatial Phenotype Associated with Extrapancreatic Perineural Invasion in Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
42949521.authors: Chen C, Yu J, Shen Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: PROPHET provides a CT-visible tumor-vessel spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI.

sections.text: Purpose To develop and evaluate an interpretable CT spatial phenotype associated with extrapancreatic perineural invasion (EPNI) in resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This multicenter study included training, internal testing, neoadjuvant testing, retrospective external testing, prospective external testing, and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA) sets. The Preoperative Risk of Perineural High-risk Extension in Tumors (PROPHET) model and threshold were locked before testing. Performance was assessed with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and threshold metrics. Six radiologists compared unaided and assisted readings. A stratified Cox model related PROPHET risk to survival, adjusting for age, sex, tumor size, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, nodal category, and differentiation. Results Among 1854 patients (median age, 63 years; 1131 male), AUCs were 0.92 (95% CI: 0.86, 0.96) in prospective external testing, 0.85 (95% CI: 0.75, 0.93) in retrospective external testing, 0.90 (95% CI: 0.83, 0.95) after neoadjuvant therapy, 0.99 (95% CI: 0.98, >0.99) in internal testing, and 0.80 (95% CI: 0.68, 0.93) in TCIA. TCIA sensitivity and specificity were 24 of 30 (80%) and two of 19 (11%). Assistance increased mean sensitivity to 93% from 82% and reduced reading time to 3.02 minutes from 3.64 minutes per patient (both Holm-adjusted P < .001). Higher PROPHET risk was associated with shorter survival (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.95; 95% CI: 1.53, 2.47; nominal P < .001). Conclusion PROPHET provides a CT-visible tumor-vessel spatial phenotype associated with pathologically confirmed EPNI.

42412178.title: Real-world evaluation of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 RLT in post-taxane mCRPC: feasibility and safety of individualized treatment in a challenging cohort.
42412178.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
42412178.journal_full: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
42412178.authors: Misirci M, Rosar F, Khreish F, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In conclusion, the retrospective real-world analysis suggests that individualized, dose-adapted 177Lu based PSMA RLT regimens may provide an opportunity to successfully extend applicability of RLT to more challenging clinical scenarios and a broader patient population without compromising safety and survival outcomes.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: Evaluating efficacy and safety of individualized [177Lu]Lu‑PSMA‑617 radioligand therapy in heavily pretreated post-taxane patients with metastatic castration‑resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), and to present a comparison with outcomes of non-individualized regimens.

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: Per‑cycle activities of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 were individualized by normalizing to body surface area and adjusting for renal clearance, hematopoietic function, and tumor burden and progression parameters. 227 post-taxane mCRPC patients with intense PSMA expression on PET/CT were enrolled in the prospective registry (REALITY; NCT04833517) and retrospectively analyzed. PSA progression-free survival (PSA-PFS) and overall survival (OS) according to Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox proportional‑hazards models with backward elimination for identification of outcome predictors, safety assessment according to CTCAE v5.0.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Median administered activity was 7.1 GBq per cycle (range 2.7-11.6 GBq) and cumulative activity 22.3 GBq (range 2.7-77.8 GBq), while patients received a median of 3 cycles within a 6-week interval. After a median follow‑up of 15.9 months (95%CI: 11.2-20.5 months), median PSA‑PFS was 5.1 months (95% CI: 4.0-6.2 months), and median OS 14.5 months (95% CI: 11.4-17.7 months). PSA declined after the first cycle in 63.9% of patients; PSA reduction ≥ 50% occurred in 51.5%. Shortened PSA‑PFS was associated with visceral metastasis (p = 0.001) and ALP ≥ 220 U/L (p = 0.004). Shortened OS was associated with visceral metastasis (p = 0.009), ALP ≥ 220 U/L (p = 0.001), age ≤ 65 years (p = 0.034), hemoglobin < 9 g/dL (p = 0.006), and early biochemical progressive disease after 1-2 courses (p < 0.001). Newly occurring or worsening hematologic or renal impairments ≥ CTCAE °3 were uncommon.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: In conclusion, the retrospective real-world analysis suggests that individualized, dose-adapted 177Lu based PSMA RLT regimens may provide an opportunity to successfully extend applicability of RLT to more challenging clinical scenarios and a broader patient population without compromising safety and survival outcomes.

42414675.title: 18F-FDG PET/MRI for non-invasive risk stratification of Intraductal Papillary Neoplasms of the Bile Duct (IPNB).
42414675.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
42414675.journal_full: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
42414675.authors: Blandino AA, Quiros E, Asmundo L, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Hybrid 18F-FDG PET/MRI shows promising potential for preoperative assessment and risk stratification of IPNBs, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: • Preoperative differentiation between dysplastic and IPNBs with invasive adenocarcinoma remains challenging, yet critical for surgical planning and prognosis. • 18F-FDG PET/MRI SUV parameters correlate with histological grade, with the lesion-to-liver SUVmax ratio showing the strongest and most robust association. • 18F-FDG PET/MRI may support non-invasive risk stratification of IPNBs, potentially overcoming the limitations associated with biopsy sampling.

sections.label: Purpose
sections.text: To evaluate the value of hybrid 18F-FDG PET/MRI in assessing the biological aggressiveness of intraductal papillary neoplasms of the bile duct (IPNBs).

sections.label: Methods
sections.text: This retrospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed IPNB who underwent 18F-FDG PET/MRI. Imaging features analyzed included 18F-FDG uptake, enhancement, diffusion restriction, duct walls infiltration, lesion size, SUVmax and lesion-to-liver SUVmax ratio. Final lesion classification was based on a composite reference standard integrating pathology with imaging follow-up, to account for potential biopsy sampling error. Spearman's correlation assessed associations between SUV parameters and histological grade. Group comparisons used the Mann-Whitney U test and Fisher's exact test. ROC analysis evaluated SUV parameters in diagnosing IPNBs with associated invasive adenocarcinoma.

sections.label: Results
sections.text: Eight patients (5 M, 3 F; median age: 65.5) with 10 lesions were included: five IPNBs with associated invasive adenocarcinoma, four dysplastic, and one non-dysplastic lesion. SUVmax and lesion-to-liver SUVmax ratio positively correlated with histological grade (ρ = 0.784, p = 0.007 and ρ = 0.844, p = 0.002, respectively). SUVmax ratio was higher in IPNBs with associated invasive adenocarcinoma versus both non-adenocarcinoma (p = 0.016) and dysplastic lesions (p = 0.032). Lesion SUVmax was higher in IPNBs with associated invasive adenocarcinoma only versus non-adenocarcinoma (p = 0.032) without reaching significance against dysplastic lesions (p = 0.063). ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0.90-0.96 (95% CI 0.674-1.000) for SUV parameters. Cut-offs of 8.04 for SUVmax and 3.00 for SUVmax ratio achieved 80% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

sections.label: Conclusion
sections.text: Hybrid 18F-FDG PET/MRI shows promising potential for preoperative assessment and risk stratification of IPNBs, warranting validation in larger prospective studies.

sections.label: Key points
sections.text: • Preoperative differentiation between dysplastic and IPNBs with invasive adenocarcinoma remains challenging, yet critical for surgical planning and prognosis. • 18F-FDG PET/MRI SUV parameters correlate with histological grade, with the lesion-to-liver SUVmax ratio showing the strongest and most robust association. • 18F-FDG PET/MRI may support non-invasive risk stratification of IPNBs, potentially overcoming the limitations associated with biopsy sampling.

42816123.title: Clinical Imaging of 225Ac in a PET Scanner via Time-of-Flight Cascade γ-Ray Imaging.
42816123.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42816123.authors: Caravaca J, Seo Y, Cabello J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: We demonstrated the feasibility of 225Ac tomography in a PET scanner via TOF-CGI, opening a window for application in other targeted radionuclide therapies. This technique enables imaging of nonpositron emitters in PET scanners and establishes an imaging paradigm complementary to SPECT. Implementation of image corrections and usage of long-axial-field-of-view PET scanners may further improve its sensitivity, resolution, and SNR.

sections.text: Clinical imaging of the α-therapy radionuclide 225Ac and its progeny has proven challenging with SPECT because of low detection efficiency and a poor signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). We propose an alternative nuclear imaging modality that enables imaging of 225Ac in PET scanners: time-of-flight cascade γ-ray imaging (TOF-CGI). Methods: We leveraged the time and position information of the γ-rays emitted in a fast cascade during the decay of 225Ac daughter 209Tl to produce 3-dimensional images of the spatial distribution of the emissions. We characterized this imaging modality with vials, evaluated it with clinical-size phantoms, and performed a pilot imaging experiment with a patient with prostate cancer injected with [225Ac]Ac-PSMA-617. Results: Imaging of vials confirmed good activity quantification linearity, minimum detectable activity of 5.5 kBq for a 20-min scan, and a spatial resolution of approximately 20 mm full width at half maximum transversally and 42 mm full width at half maximum axially. A phantom filled with a concentration of 44 kBq/mL revealed a higher SNR than did SPECT with a 10-fold-shorter scan time. The TOF-CGI sensitivity with the phantom was 26.0 cps/MBq, and the detection efficiency was an order of magnitude higher with TOF-CGI than with SPECT. TOF-CGI of the patient demonstrated activity within a known tumor in the prostate bed and higher SNR than that of SPECT. Conclusion: We demonstrated the feasibility of 225Ac tomography in a PET scanner via TOF-CGI, opening a window for application in other targeted radionuclide therapies. This technique enables imaging of nonpositron emitters in PET scanners and establishes an imaging paradigm complementary to SPECT. Implementation of image corrections and usage of long-axial-field-of-view PET scanners may further improve its sensitivity, resolution, and SNR.

42816125.title: Fully Automated Segmentation of [18F]FDG and [68Ga]/[18F]PSMA PET/CT Images via Data-Centric Deep Learning.
42816125.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42816125.authors: Pires M, Gutschmayer S, Bergalla E, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: LION enables PET-only automated segmentation for [18F]FDG and PSMA-targeted PET. Training data composition, particularly spatial diversity quantified by TOMs, was strongly associated with segmentation performance.

sections.text: The purpose of this study was to develop and validate lesion identification in oncologic nuclear imaging (LION), an open-source PET-only tumor segmentation pipeline for [18F]FDG and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted PET/CT, and to investigate how training data characteristics influence segmentation performance. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter study, 5209 [18F]FDG PET/CT scans spanning 19 disease types and 2046 PSMA-targeted PET/CT scans were used to train PET-only segmentation models. Tumor segmentation incorporated organs with physiologic uptake as auxiliary classes to enable PET-only inference. Tumor occurrence maps (TOMs) quantified tumor spatial diversity across the training data. For [18F]FDG, disease-specific and mixed-disease models trained on progressively larger subsets were compared to test whether increasing spatial diversity improves generalization. Scanner-related domain shift was analyzed using DINOv2 embeddings. Models were evaluated on multicenter holdout cohorts (616 [18F]FDG scans across 4 diseases; 443 PSMA-targeted prostate cancer scans) and compared with 3 open-source tools. Results: Organ context improved median Dice from 0.62 to 0.71 for [18F]FDG and from 0.75 to 0.83 for PSMA, on the complete holdout cohorts. Spatial diversity measured by TOMs was strongly associated with Dice (Spearman ρ = 0.80, P = 0.003). A mixed-disease model trained on 500 patients matched the performance of a lymphoma specialist model trained on 3031 cases. DINOv2 embeddings revealed scanner-induced domain shift between same-disease cohorts. LION achieved median Dice scores of 0.71 for [18F]FDG and 0.85 for PSMA and outperformed other open-source approaches on the model-comparison test set, which excluded the AutoPET test cases. Conclusion: LION enables PET-only automated segmentation for [18F]FDG and PSMA-targeted PET. Training data composition, particularly spatial diversity quantified by TOMs, was strongly associated with segmentation performance.

42850038.title: 68Ga-Labeled Dimeric Cyclic Peptide for Nectin-4-Targeted PET Imaging: From Preclinical Evaluation to First-in-Human Imaging in Breast Cancer.
42850038.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42850038.authors: Ge S, Li J, Shi J, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 was a clinically translatable nectin-4-targeted PET tracer with high affinity, favorable pharmacokinetics, and specific tumor uptake. Preclinical and pilot clinical results supported further clinical evaluation of [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 for noninvasive imaging of nectin-4 expression, particularly for assessment of metastatic disease.

sections.text: Nectin-4 is an attractive target for molecular imaging and targeted therapy because of its overexpression in multiple malignancies. We developed a nectin cell adhesion molecule 4 (nectin-4)-targeted 68Ga-labeled dimeric cyclic peptide PET tracer, [68Ga]Ga-TDN1, for noninvasive imaging of nectin-4 expression. Methods: TDN1 was generated by click chemistry to conjugate 2 nectin-4-binding bicyclic peptides and was radiolabeled with 68Ga. Binding affinity was assessed by surface plasmon resonance. Target specificity and tumor-targeting ability were evaluated by cell uptake, blocking, small-animal PET/CT, and biodistribution studies in nectin-4-positive and nectin-4-negative tumor models. [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 was further compared with [68Ga]Ga-N188 in preclinical models. After preclinical evaluation, [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 PET/CT was investigated in a pilot first-in-human study in 6 patients with breast cancer and directly compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. Results: TDN1 showed high affinity for nectin-4 (K D = 1.92 × 10-10 M). In preclinical studies, [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 showed specific uptake in nectin-4-positive cells and tumors, low uptake in nectin-4-negative models, and marked reduction in uptake under blocking conditions. Compared with [68Ga]Ga-N188, [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 showed higher tumor uptake and longer retention across multiple nectin-4-positive xenografts. In the pilot clinical study, [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 was well-tolerated and showed favorable biodistribution and dosimetry. [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 PET/CT revealed imaging performance comparable to that of [18F]FDG PET/CT for primary tumors and most nodal metastases and demonstrated higher uptake and improved lesion detection in bone and liver metastases in selected patients. [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 was a clinically translatable nectin-4-targeted PET tracer with high affinity, favorable pharmacokinetics, and specific tumor uptake. Preclinical and pilot clinical results supported further clinical evaluation of [68Ga]Ga-TDN1 for noninvasive imaging of nectin-4 expression, particularly for assessment of metastatic disease.

42850042.title: Preclinical Evaluation on the Radiohybrid Tandem [18F]La- and [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 for Targeted α-Therapy of Prostate Cancer.
42850042.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42850042.authors: Sun B, Werner D, Ni J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1/[18F]La-rhPSMA-10.1 represents a promising theranostic pair that may improve patient selection and dosimetry of α-therapy for prostate cancer.

sections.text: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted α-therapy holds promise for the treatment of prostate cancer but has increased side effects compared with therapy using β-emitting PSMA ligands. This emphasizes the need for precise imaging of the biodistribution of 225Ac-labeled ligands for patient selection and dosimetry. However, imaging of [225Ac]Ac-PSMA ligands remains technically challenging, and no radioactive actinium isotopes with favorable imaging characteristics exist. In this study, we therefore developed radiohybrid ligands that can be labeled with 225Ac for therapy and 18F for imaging. Methods: We developed the radiohybrid ligand pair [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 and [18F]La-rhPSMA-10.1. Lanthanum was used for the diagnostic agent because no stable actinium isotopes exist, and the ionic chemistry of lanthanum and actinium is similar. The PSMA binding affinity, cellular internalization, and externalization of the ligands were determined. Biodistribution studies of [18F]La-rhPSMA-10.1 and [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 versus the reference [225Ac]Ac-PSMA I&T were performed in LNCaP tumor-bearing mice. For evaluation of the efficacy, LNCaP tumor-bearing mice (n = 6 per group) received a single dose of [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 or [225Ac]Ac-PSMA I&T or no treatment. Results: [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 and [18F]La-rhPSMA-10.1 showed similar cellular uptake parameters and a similar biodistribution. Compared with [225Ac]Ac-PSMA I&T, tumor uptake of [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 was 2.2-fold and 3.5-fold higher at 1 h and 24 h postinjection, respectively, with a similar biodistribution in healthy tissues. In the efficacy study, median survival was 12 d in the control group and more than 50 d for animals treated with [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 or [225Ac]Ac-PSMA I&T. Tumor growth was similarly inhibited by [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1 or [225Ac]Ac-PSMA I&T. Conclusion: [225Ac]Ac-rhPSMA-10.1/[18F]La-rhPSMA-10.1 represents a promising theranostic pair that may improve patient selection and dosimetry of α-therapy for prostate cancer.

42850043.title: [68Ga]Ga-SSO120 PET/CT Imaging in Pediatric Patients with Neuroblastoma: Biodistribution and Whole-Body Radiation Dosimetry.
42850043.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42850043.authors: Teles L, van Rooij R, van Noesel MM, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: [68Ga]Ga-SSO120 PET/CT was safe in pediatric patients with neuroblastoma, with a low effective radiation dose, and detected neuroblastoma lesions with a good target-to-noise ratio. Image acquisition at 30 and 60 min postinjection seemed equivalent.

sections.text: The clinical standard for neuroblastoma detection is based on targeting the norepinephrine transporter with [123I]MIBG, which has several challenges. Imaging the somatostatin receptor (SSTR) is a strong alternative. In contrast to standard DOTATATE, SSTR antagonist imaging with [68Ga]Ga-satoreotide trizoxetan ([68Ga]-SSO120) can potentially improve lesion detection as it targets both active and inactive SSTRs. We present the biodistribution and radiation exposure results of [68Ga]Ga-SSO120 PET/CT imaging in pediatric patients with neuroblastoma. Methods: Patients age 3-7 y with stage 4 neuroblastoma received 2 MBq/kg of [68Ga]Ga-SSO120, followed by a 60-min dynamic scan and a static PET/CT scan. SUV normalized to lean body mass (SULmax, SULmean, SULpeak) and time-activity curves were measured for suspected lesions and various tissue compartments. Tumor-to-liver and tumor-to-blood pool ratios were calculated. Radiation doses to various organs and the total-body effective dose were computed. Results: Five patients underwent dynamic [68Ga]Ga-SSO120 PET/CT scanning, with a total of 17 neuroblastoma lesions. The median administered activity was 2.5 MBq/kg (range, 2.1-2.8 MBq/kg). At 60 min postinjection, the median tumor SULmax and SULpeak were 4.28 (range, 1.89-18.07) and 2.71 (range, 1.23-14.77), respectively, and the median tumor-to-liver ratio was 4.05. The highest exposure was in the bladder (22.3 ± 4.3 μSv/MBq). The effective dose was 0.088 ± 0.014 mSv/MBq. Conclusion: [68Ga]Ga-SSO120 PET/CT was safe in pediatric patients with neuroblastoma, with a low effective radiation dose, and detected neuroblastoma lesions with a good target-to-noise ratio. Image acquisition at 30 and 60 min postinjection seemed equivalent.

42850044.title: β-Cell Mass and Function, Pancreatic Volume, and Fat Differences Between Short- and Long-Duration Type 1 Diabetes: A Detailed PET/CT Imaging Study.
42850044.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42850044.authors: Tokgöz S, de Groen P, Jansen TJP, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: This study offers insights in the potential of imaging markers together with function tests to monitor disease progression and may offer valuable information for the timing to restore β-cell function or to slow down β-cell destruction.

sections.text: People with recent-onset diabetes often have preserved C-peptide production, which tends to decline during the first 7 y after diagnosis and stabilizes thereafter. Whether this holds true for β-cell mass is unknown. In this pooled post hoc analysis, we aimed to investigate total β-cell mass in individuals with short- and long-duration type 1 diabetes. Methods: Data of 16 individuals with short- (<7 y) and 10 with long-duration type 1 diabetes (≥7 y) who underwent [68Ga]Ga-NODAGA-exendin-4 PET/CT and mixed-meal tolerance test were used to determine total β-cell mass and function, respectively. Intrapancreatic fat deposition and pancreatic volume were derived from CT. Results: Total β-cell mass was higher in individuals with short-duration type 1 diabetes compared with those with long-duration type 1 diabetes (4.4 ± 1.8 vs. 2.8 ± 1.3 kBq/MBq, P = 0.012). Larger pancreatic volume, lower intrapancreatic fat deposition, and higher β-cell function were observed in individuals with short-duration type 1 diabetes compared with the long-duration group. Total β-cell mass positively correlated with β-cell function (r = 0.46, P = 0.019) and pancreatic volume (r = 0.91, P < 0.0001) and inversely correlated with body mass index (r = -0.61, P = 0.0009). Conclusion: This study offers insights in the potential of imaging markers together with function tests to monitor disease progression and may offer valuable information for the timing to restore β-cell function or to slow down β-cell destruction.

42880958.title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in Refractory Meningiomas: Results from the French Multicenter MELUTE Cohort.
42880958.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42880958.authors: Garabedian N, Zaragori T, Tabouret E, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

sections.text: Evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas derives mainly from small, single-center studies. The French national multicenter MELUTE study aimed to consolidate these data using a standardized regimen within a compassionate-use program approved by a national multidisciplinary tumor board. Methods: In this retrospective multicenter cohort study, patients with refractory meningiomas treated with [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in 18 French centers between July 2022 and December 2024 were included. Treatment consisted of 7.4 GBq every 8 wk for up to 4 cycles. Clinical data (demographics, histologic World Health Organization grade [WHO], prior treatments, number of cycles, toxicity, progression, survival status as of October 1, 2025) were collected. Baseline [68Ga]Ga-DOTATOC PET and brain MRI scans obtained before and after treatment were centrally reviewed. The primary endpoint was 6-mo progression-free survival (PFS) assessed using volumetric Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology Group criteria. Secondary endpoints were PFS, overall survival (OS), and safety. Results: Sixty-nine patients were included (mean age, 65.1 ± 13.2 y; 52% female): 13 WHO grade 1, 42 WHO grade 2, 8 WHO grade 3, and 6 without histology. Most had prior surgery (86%) or radiotherapy (93%); 32% received prior systemic therapy. Twelve patients (17%) did not complete 4 cycles; only one discontinuation was toxicity-related. Six-month PFS was 70% (95% CI, 58.7-80.4%). Median PFS was 14.6 mo (95% CI, 13.3-18.5 mo), and median OS was 27.6 mo (95% CI, 24.2 mo to not reached). Grade 3 adverse events, mainly lymphopenia, occurred in 16%. Meningioma WHO grade independently predicted PFS, whereas higher Karnofsky performance status and corticosteroid use were protective; worse OS was associated with higher baseline tumor growth rate and prior systemic therapy. Conclusion: MELUTE demonstrates promising efficacy and favorable safety of [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE in refractory meningiomas with limited therapeutic options.

42880959.title: Brain-Specific Quantification of Somatostatin Receptor Expression: SUVmax and SUVRsss as Quantitative Correlates of the Krenning Score in Meningioma.
42880959.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42880959.authors: Marulanda-Corzo V, Farid M, Hill T, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: SUVRsss and SUVmax are complementary quantitative correlates of Krenning scores 2-4 in [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET-visible, MRI-measurable meningiomas. Brain-only PET evaluation may provide an alternative to liver- and spleen-based visual grading and reduce the need for whole-body imaging in selected settings. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve-derived SUV thresholds correspond to Krenning scores used for eligibility for treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, supporting further evaluation of quantitative PET parameters for theranostic decision-making for patients with meningioma.

sections.text: Somatostatin receptor type 2 is highly expressed in meningiomas and can be quantified using [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET. The Krenning score, originally developed for [111In]In-octreotide scintigraphy, remains the standard visual grading system for somatostatin receptor expression and is widely used to guide eligibility for peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. However, visual grading may not optimally translate to intracranial disease. This study evaluated the relationship between brain-specific quantitative PET parameters-SUVmax and SUV ratio normalized to the superior sagittal sinus (SUVRsss)-and the Krenning score in meningioma. Methods: This single-institution retrospective study included 44 patients (70 meningiomas) who underwent clinical vertex-to-thigh [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT. Quantitative parameters (SUVmax, SUVRsss, lesion size) were extracted from coregistered PET and MR images. Spearman rank correlation analysis was performed to assess associations between imaging variables and Krenning score. Differences in quantitative PET parameters across Krenning categories were evaluated using Kruskal-Wallis test and Holm-Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U test. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve analysis using the Youden J index identified optimal cutoffs for clinically relevant thresholds (Krenning score of <3 vs. ≥3 and 3 vs. 4). Results: SUVRsss and SUVmax were strongly correlated with the Krenning score (SUVRsss: Spearman ρ = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.55-0.82; SUVmax: Spearman ρ = 0.77; 95% CI, 0.64-0.85; P < 0.0001). PET parameters differed significantly across Krenning categories (all P < 0.001). SUVRsss optimal thresholds were 9.00 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.86; 95% CI, 0.74-0.96) for Krenning scores of 2 versus 3 and 29.84 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.93-1.00) for Krenning scores of 3 versus 4. SUVmax optimal thresholds were 7.20 (AUC, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.84-0.99) and 30.70 (AUC, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.95-1.00), respectively. Conclusion: SUVRsss and SUVmax are complementary quantitative correlates of Krenning scores 2-4 in [68Ga]Ga-DOTATATE PET-visible, MRI-measurable meningiomas. Brain-only PET evaluation may provide an alternative to liver- and spleen-based visual grading and reduce the need for whole-body imaging in selected settings. Receiver-operating-characteristic curve-derived SUV thresholds correspond to Krenning scores used for eligibility for treatment with peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, supporting further evaluation of quantitative PET parameters for theranostic decision-making for patients with meningioma.

42880965.title: Multimodal Visual Question Answering System for Survival Prognosis in PSMA-Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Therapy.
42880965.journal_full: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
42880965.authors: Kassar M, Hu J, Rauscher I, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: By adopting a physician-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning. The preliminary results indicate that VQA-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.

sections.text: Large language models show great promise for clinical decision support but generally lack medical imaging integration. Therefore, vision-language models have been proposed, but there is little evidence on their performance, particularly compared with conventional machine learning. Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy is a well-established treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), but it is still not known which patients will be good long-term responders. Therefore, this study proposes a physician-inspired visual question answering (VQA) framework that emulates the structured integration of PSMA-directed imaging and clinical data used in routine clinical assessment for overall survival prognostication. Methods: As a proof of concept, we conducted a retrospective, multicenter study across 2 academic institutions that included 110 patients with mCRPC who were treated with either [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T or [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617. Our VQA approach incorporates a 3-dimensional image encoder, the domain-specific language model RadBERT, and a cross-modal transformer to process baseline and interim (after 2 cycles) PET and SPECT images, clinical data, and clinical query. The model was trained to predict 24-mo survival, and performance was compared with state-of-the-art approaches. External validation was performed with the [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 cohort. Results: The VQA model outperformed all state-of-the-art approaches while showing accuracy comparable to the query-free attention multimodal fusion model. Specifically, it achieved 81.8% accuracy (95% CI, 0.52-0.95) when integrating SPECT or PET images with prostate-specific antigen measurements. External validation of the VQA showed 71.9% accuracy (95% CI, 0.53-0.86) after few-shot fine-tuning, with further improvement over all state-of-the-art approaches in survival stratification. The VQA approach showed the closest calibration with the ground-truth survival distribution, with no significant differences observed (log-rank test, P = 0.76). Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed the highest area under the curve (0.75) among the evaluated models. Together, these findings suggest that the VQA approach demonstrated adaptability across different PSMA ligands while maintaining slightly improved yet comparable overall survival prognostic performance. Conclusion: By adopting a physician-inspired assessment workflow, the VQA framework shows advantages in integrating imaging and laboratory data for clinical decision support compared with conventional machine learning. The preliminary results indicate that VQA-based approaches warrant future evaluation for survival prognostication in patients with mCRPC who are receiving PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy.
